The video begins with a black screen showing a brief blip of white text. It then transitions to a green-toned graphic of a person's profile, presumably a man, with only the side of his face and part of his shoulder visible. Overlayed on this image is the white text "MMH MUSEUM OF MEDIA HISTORY" along with an icon resembling a sun or a star made of short, white lines. Below this, there is another line of text that reads "SPECIAL PROJECTS DIVISION Tampa Bay Federal District, Florida." The transition to a black screen then occurs, as a voice over begins to narrate the media landscape. The narrator describes how the press as it was, has since ceased to exist. Additionally, the narrator describes news organizations as an after thought. As the narrator speaks, a white fuzzy blob appears on screen and transforms in to different shapes as the narration continues.

The video segment starts with a black screen, leading into the speaker describing the events of 2014 which began in the mid-20th century. In black and white, we see a man with thinning hair, dressed in a black suit, white collared shirt, and red tie sitting at a table, looking into the camera. The speaker explains that in 1989 Tim Berners-Lee, a computer scientist at the CERN Particle Physics Laboratory in Switzerland, invented the World Wide Web. Next, we see “2021” in large white text. The speaker then describes that in 1990, Amazon.com was founded. The Amazon logo appears in grey on a black background, with the text “amazon.com” and the curved arrow from A to Z under the name, representing Amazon’s claim to sell everything. He explains that the young creator dreamt of a store that sold everything. In 1998, the video continues to narrate that two Stanford programmers created Google. The video then shows the word "Google" in grey lettering on a black background.

The video segment begins with a grayscale rendering of the word "Google" centered on a black background. This transitions into a series of Google search results related to the word "Google." Text from the search results includes phrases like "Writing for Google," "Google - Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia," and various URLs and dates, primarily from 2004. The segment then cuts to a grayscale image of the TiVo logo, which is a stylized TV set with the word "TiVo" written inside, along with a smiley face. The image is rough, resembling a sketch or low-resolution rendering. The text beneath the logo states "In 1999, TiVo transforms television by unshackling it from the constraints of time."

The video begins with the iconic title "The New York Times" displayed in white old English font against a black background. An audio narration comments on the newspaper's decision to become a print-only newsletter, positioning it as a protest against Google's "hegemony" and catering specifically to an "elite and elderly" audience. The visuals then fade to a dark green screen displaying a copyright notice: "(C) 2014 MUSEUM OF MEDIA HISTORY." A final dark green screen then shows the text "Written by Robin Sloan and Matt Thompson, Narration by Matt Thompson, Music by Minus Kelvin, Flash production by Robin Sloan." The font used is a simple typewriter style in white. There are no people visible in the video. The transitions are simple fades between the black, dark green and dark green screen. The overall tone is a satirical commentary on the changing landscape of news media and the perceived resistance of traditional institutions like the New York Times to digital dominance.
